<!--
Authoring note: always leave a blank line between a description and the code chunk
that draws its plot. knitr writes a plot as an inline image, so a chunk opened directly
after a text line puts the image into the same paragraph as the text, and the browser
may then lay the plot out next to the description instead of below it.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Natural (numeric-aware) ordering of sample names, e.g. S1, S2, ..., S9, S10,
# S11 rather than the lexicographic S1, S10, S11, S2, ... Defined in base R so
# it works regardless of which packages the report container provides.
natural_sort <- function(x) {
    x <- as.character(x)
    digit_runs <- regmatches(x, gregexpr("[0-9]+", x))
    all_digits <- unlist(digit_runs)
    pad_width <- if (length(all_digits)) max(nchar(all_digits)) else 0L
    key <- x
    regmatches(key, gregexpr("[0-9]+", key)) <- lapply(
        digit_runs,
        function(d) formatC(as.integer(d), width = pad_width, flag = "0"))
    x[order(key)]
}
```

# Results of CAGEr analysis

## Raw reads
These QC plots show the status of the data before normalization or filtering.

### Tag region annotation
Annotation of raw reads (tags) per sample.
Tags are not filtered, and tag counts are not normalized yet.
It is expected to see more intergenic tags here than after filtering and clustering which removes much of the noise.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
options(warn=-1)
sampleNs <- unname(CAGEr::sampleLabels(ce))
tagannot_plot <- readRDS("tag_region_annotation_plot.rds")
tagannot_plot + ggplot2::xlim(rev(natural_sort(unique(sampleNs))))
```

### Correlation of samples at the raw tag count level
Pairwise correlation of samples by raw tag counts per TSS (also known as "CTSS" for "CAGE TSS").
For each pair of samples, a TSS is included in the correlation calculation if its raw tag count reaches the threshold `corrplot_tagCountThreshold` in at least one of the two samples.
The sample correlation plot is for diagnostic purposes, such as highlighting batch effects.
The self-correlation diagonal runs from the top-right to the bottom-left cell.
The `corrplot_tagCountThreshold` is shared with correlation plots further below.
For a higher-resolution plot, check the PDF file saved in the `results/cager/plots` folder.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
print(paste0("The current corrplot_tagCountThreshold value is: ", corrplot_tagCountThreshold))

corr_m <- readRDS("CTSS_correlations_matrix.rds")
sample_size <- dim(corr_m)[1]
heatmap_cex <- sample_size^(-0.2)
hm_plot <- readRDS("CTSS_correlations_plot.rds")
eval(hm_plot$call)
```

## Normalization
Next, tag counts are normalized.

### Power-law distributions
Number of CAGE tags versus number of TSSs supported by at least as many tags [should follow the power-law distribution](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/gb-2009-10-7-r79).
The power-law distribution is fitted in the range between the two dotted lines (both boundaries included).
The positions of the dotted lines are modifiable by the user with the `norm_range_min` and `norm_range_max` parameters.
The total number of tags `t_norm` defaults to 1,000,000, which corresponds to TPM, but in the case of very deep sequencing it should be adjusted.

The reference power-law distribution, to which all samples are normalized, is fully defined by two values: `alpha`, which is the slope of the distribution on the log-log plot taken with the opposite sign, and `T`, the total number of tags in the distribution.
CAGEr fits a power law to each sample within the fitting range and shows the resulting per-sample `alpha` values in the plot legend. The plot subtitle and the grey dashed line show the reference distribution that CAGEr suggests: its `alpha` is the median of the per-sample values and its `T` is a power of ten closest to the median number of tags per sample.
Both values can be set by the user. If the `alpha` parameter is provided, it is used for normalization instead of the fitted median (the plot still shows the fitted one). `T` is always taken from the `t_norm` parameter: the `T` suggested on the plot only positions the dashed reference line and is not used for normalization.

The reverse-cumulative plot below is generated on raw (un-normalized) tag counts.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
print(paste0("The current norm_range_min value is: ", norm_range_min))
print(paste0("The current norm_range_max value is: ", norm_range_max))
print(paste0("The current normalization method (norm_method) is: ", norm_method))
print(paste0("The current t_norm value is: ", t_norm))
print(paste0("The user-provided alpha value is: ", alpha, ". If this value is null, the calculated value shown on the plot is used for normalization: it is the median of the per-sample fitted alphas. Whether fitted or provided by the user, alpha is never allowed to be less than 1.05: a smaller value is replaced by 1.05."))

revc_plot <- readRDS("reverse_cumulative_plot.rds")
revc_plot
```

The reverse-cumulative plot below is generated on the power-law-normalized tag counts.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
revc_norm_plot <- readRDS("reverse_cumulative_normalized_plot.rds")
revc_norm_plot
```

### Correlations of samples at the normalized tag count level
Pairwise correlation of samples by normalized tag counts per TSS.
For each pair of samples, a TSS is included in the correlation calculation if its normalized tag count reaches the threshold `corrplot_tagCountThreshold` in at least one of the two samples.
The plot is for diagnostic purposes, such as highlighting batch effects.
Normalization should have removed batch effects to some extent.
The self-correlation diagonal runs from the top-right to the bottom-left cell.
For a higher-resolution plot, check the PDF file saved in the `results/cager/plots` folder.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
print(paste0("The current corrplot_tagCountThreshold value is: ", corrplot_tagCountThreshold))

corr_m <- readRDS("norm_CTSS_correlations_matrix.rds")
sample_size <- dim(corr_m)[1]
heatmap_cex <- sample_size^(-0.2)
hm_plot <- readRDS("norm_CTSS_correlations_plot.rds")
eval(hm_plot$call)
```

### PCA plot of samples, based on normalized tag counts
PCA was run on all samples, using the top 500 most variable TSSs, according to normalised tag counts (TPM). 
If fewer than 500 TSSs are available, all TSSs are used.
The variance explained by each principal component is shown in parentheses.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
pca_plot <- readRDS("CTSS_pca_plot.rds")
pca_plot
```

## Tag clustering
After normalization, tag clusters are identified with the following parameters.
Before clustering, low-expressed TSSs are filtered by the user-defined thresholds: `sample_num_thr` and `ctss_thr`.
A TSS is kept (as a high-fidelity TSS) if its normalized expression is strictly greater than `ctss_thr` TPM in at least `sample_num_thr` samples (if `sample_num_thr` exceeds the number of samples, all samples are required).
By default, these values are 1 sample and 1 TPM, meaning that the high-fidelity TSSs have more than 1 TPM in at least one sample.

The clustering is done using the distance-based distclu method.
The max distance is a user-defined parameter `distclu_maxDist`: TSSs that are at most `distclu_maxDist` bp apart are joined into the same tag cluster.

With the `keepSingletonsAbove` parameter, the user can decide the TPM threshold at or above which even a single TSS is kept as a tag cluster.

The `iq_low` and `iq_high` parameters are used to define the lower and upper quantile boundaries of the interquantile range within which the majority of the signal lies.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
print(paste0("The current sample_num_thr value is: ", sample_num_thr))
print(paste0("The current ctss_thr value is: ", ctss_thr))
print(paste0("The current distclu_maxDist value is: ", distclu_maxDist))
print(paste0("The current keepSingletonsAbove value is: ", keepSingletonsAbove))

print(paste0("The current iq_low value is: ", iq_low))
print(paste0("The current iq_high value is: ", iq_high))
```

### Tag cluster interquantile width
Interquantile width (IQW) distribution in each sample, for tag clusters with expression of at least `iqw_tpm_threshold` TPM, as set by the user.
A sequencing library of sufficient depth shows two types of tag clusters (narrow and broad) as two peaks in the IQW distribution: a high peak on the left (narrow clusters) and a broad peak on the right (broad clusters).
In low-depth samples, the broad type may be lacking, which flags low-quality data.

```{r iqw-layout, include=FALSE}
iqw_plot <- readRDS("interquantile_width_tagclusters_plot.rds")

# CAGEr facets this plot with the ggplot2 default layout, which spreads the
# panels over roughly as many columns as rows. With many samples that makes the
# individual panels too small to read, so cap the grid at three columns and grow
# the figure vertically instead. With three or fewer samples this is the same
# single-row layout as before.
iqw_n_samples <- length(unique(as.character(iqw_plot$data$sampleName)))
iqw_ncol <- min(3L, max(1L, iqw_n_samples))
iqw_nrow <- ceiling(iqw_n_samples / iqw_ncol)
iqw_fig_height <- max(5, 2.2 * iqw_nrow)
```

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE, fig.height=iqw_fig_height}
print(paste0("The current iqw_tpm_threshold value is: ", iqw_tpm_threshold))

iqw_plot + ggplot2::facet_wrap("~sampleName", ncol = iqw_ncol)
```

### Number of tag clusters per sample
This plot shows the number of tag clusters identified in each sample.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
tag_clusters_count_plot <- readRDS("tag_clusters_counts_plot.rds")
tag_clusters_count_plot
```

### Tag cluster annotation
ChIPseeker annotation of genomic regions where tag clusters reside.
The region labels are extracted from a TxDb object generated from the GTF file provided by the user.
You can find this file in the `results/txdb` folder.
Two parameters should be defined for the annotation: `tssregion_up` and `tssregion_down`.
They correspond to the upstream and downstream distance from the TSS of *an annotated* transcript to include into the TSS region for the ChIPseeker annotation.
`tssregion_up` should be negative, `tssregion_down` should be positive.
These parameters are shared with the enhancer annotation.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
print(paste0("The current tssregion_up value is: ", tssregion_up))
print(paste0("The current tssregion_down value is: ", tssregion_down))

sampleNs <- unname(CAGEr::sampleLabels(ce))
chta_plot <- readRDS("chipseeker_tagCluster_annotation_plot.rds")
chta_plot + ggplot2::xlim(rev(natural_sort(unique(sampleNs))))
```

### Dinucleotide frequencies in tag clusters, weighted by expression (TPM)
The plot below is based on the **dominant TSSs** of the tag clusters obtained above. 
For each unique dinucleotide, it shows the proportion of the total normalised **dominant TSS** expression, per sample.
Dinucleotides are sorted by the median of their per-sample proportions, in decreasing order: the highest median comes first, at the top of the bar plot or on the left of the heatmap that replaces it when there are more than 10 samples.

```{r dinuc-style, include=FALSE}
# The two dinucleotide plots below are drawn as a bar plot (up to 10 samples) or
# as a heatmap (more than 10 samples). The bar plot uses coord_flip(), so the
# dinucleotide names sit on the vertical axis there and on the horizontal axis
# in the heatmap. style_dinuc() shrinks the plot down to report size while
# keeping the dinucleotide names, the legend title and entries, the axis titles
# and (in the bar plot) the proportion axis numbers big enough to read, and drops the
# plot title, since the text above each plot already says what it shows.
style_dinuc <- function(p) {
    small <- ggplot2::element_text(size = 5)
    labels <- ggplot2::element_text(size = 11, colour = "black")
    titles <- ggplot2::element_text(size = 12)
    flipped <- inherits(p$coordinates, "CoordFlip")
    p + ggplot2::ggtitle(NULL) + ggplot2::theme(
        text = small,
        axis.text.x = if (flipped) {
            ggplot2::element_text(angle = 90, size = 11, colour = "black")
        } else {
            ggplot2::element_text(angle = 90, size = 11, colour = "black")
        },
        axis.text.y = if (flipped) labels else small,
        axis.title.x = titles,
        axis.title.y = titles,
        legend.title = titles,
        legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11))
}
```
```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
dinucl_plot <- readRDS("dinucleotide_frequencies_plot.rds")
style_dinuc(dinucl_plot)
```

The plot below is based on **all high-fidelity TSSs**: those expressed at TPM strictly greater than `ctss_thr` in at least `sample_num_thr` samples (the same low-expression filter used before tag clustering).
For each unique dinucleotide, it shows the proportion of the total normalised **high-fidelity TSS** expression, per sample.
Dinucleotides are sorted by the median of their per-sample proportions, in decreasing order: the highest median comes first, at the top of the bar plot or on the left of the heatmap that replaces it when there are more than 10 samples.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
print(paste0("The current ctss_thr value is: ", ctss_thr))
print(paste0("The current sample_num_thr value is: ", sample_num_thr))

dinucl_all_plot <- readRDS("dinucleotide_frequencies_all_tss_plot.rds")
style_dinuc(dinucl_all_plot)
```

### TSS region logos

```{r logo_setup, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
logo_samples <- natural_sort(unname(CAGEr::sampleLabels(ce)))
n_logo_samples <- length(logo_samples)
# Show the logos in the report only when there are at most 60 samples.
# Otherwise there would be too many to display, and the user is pointed to the
# individual files saved on disk.
show_logos <- n_logo_samples <= 60
# Number of columns the logos are arranged in: 1 column for up to 5 samples,
# 2 columns for 6 to 29 samples and 3 columns for 30 to 60 samples.
logo_n_cols <- if (n_logo_samples <= 5) {
    1
} else if (n_logo_samples <= 29) {
    2
} else {
    3
}
logo_out_width <- paste0(floor(100 / logo_n_cols), "%")
```
```{r logo_text, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (show_logos) {
    cat(paste0(
        "Shown below are the per-sample logos of the dominant TSS regions of ",
        "tag clusters that are annotated as promoters. The number of bases ",
        "included upstream of the dominant TSS is set by the user with the ",
        "tsslogo_upstream parameter."))
} else {
    cat(paste0(
        "There are ", n_logo_samples, " samples, which is too many to display ",
        "the dominant TSS region logos in this report. Instead, the per-sample ", 
        "dominant TSS region logos of ",
        "the tag clusters that are annotated as promoters are ",
        "saved separately in the results/cager/plots folder, where they can be ",
        "viewed individually. The number of bases included upstream of the ",
        "dominant TSS is set by the user with the tsslogo_upstream parameter."))
}
```
```{r logo_param, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
print(paste0("The current tsslogo_upstream value is: ", tsslogo_upstream))
```
```{r logo_plots, eval=show_logos, include=show_logos, echo=FALSE, fig.show='hold', out.width=logo_out_width, fig.height=3.33}
for (logo_sample in logo_samples) {
    print(readRDS(paste0(
        logo_sample, "_tagcluster_dominantTSSlogos_plot.rds")))
}
```

## Consensus clustering
To compare the activity of tag clusters between samples, consensus clusters are defined.
Consensus clusters are clusters aggregated from tag clusters of different samples which are in close vicinity and pass a TPM threshold: tag clusters with an expression of at least `consensus_thr` TPM are used, and those whose interquantile ranges (widths) are at most `consensus_dist` bp apart are merged into one consensus cluster.
The TPM threshold and the maximum distance between the interquantile ranges of tag clusters can be set by the user with the `consensus_thr` and `consensus_dist` parameters, respectively.
The per-sample expression of a consensus cluster is the total expression of its high-fidelity TSSs that are expressed strictly greater than `consensus_thr` TPM in at least one sample.

The `cons_full_span` parameter controls whether the `iq_low` and `iq_high` boundaries (defined in the [Tag clustering](#tag-clustering) section above) are also applied when tag clusters are aggregated into consensus clusters.
When `cons_full_span` is *false* (the default), the interquantile range delimited by `iq_low` and `iq_high` is used for consensus cluster calling.
When `cons_full_span` is *true*, `iq_low` and `iq_high` are not used for consensus cluster calling and the whole span of the tag clusters is taken into account when they are aggregated.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
print(paste0("The current consensus_dist value is: ", consensus_dist))
print(paste0("The current consensus_thr value is: ", consensus_thr))
print(paste0("The current cons_full_span value is: ", cons_full_span))
```

### Number of non-zero consensus clusters
This plot shows the number of non-zero consensus clusters per sample, as well as the total number of consensus clusters (union).
A consensus cluster is non-zero in a sample if it is expressed in that sample.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
cc_plot <- readRDS("consensus_counts_plot.rds")
cc_plot
```

### Consensus cluster PCA
PCA of samples, calculated on the TPM values of the top 500 most variable consensus clusters across samples (if fewer than 500 consensus clusters are available, all of them are used).
The variance explained by each principal component is shown in parentheses.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
ccp_plot <- readRDS("consensus_clusters_pca_plot.rds")
ccp_plot
```

## Enhancer calling
Enahncers are defined as sites with balanced bidirectional transcription.
The balance threshold is a user-defined parameter `cfBalanceThreshold`: a site is called bidirectional if its balance score is strictly greater than `cfBalanceThreshold`.
The normalized TPM values of TSSs are used as input for enhancer calling.
The threshold for these TPM values is set by the user with the `unexpressed` parameter: only the TSSs with TPM values strictly greater than `unexpressed` count as expressed.
Enhancers are called on expressed TSS values summed over all samples, but only those enhancers are kept that have support in at least a user-defined number of samples `minSamples`. 
A sample supports an enhancer if the enhancer's TSS expression is above `unexpressed` TPM on both strands.
To ensure that promoters are not confused with enhancers, any enhancer region overlapping consensus clusters is removed.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
print(paste0("The current cfBalanceThreshold value is: ", cfBalanceThreshold))
print(paste0("The current unexpressed value is: ", unexpressed))
print(paste0("The current minSamples value is: ", minSamples))
```

### Number of active enhancers per sample
This plot shows the number of active enhancers per sample, as well as the total number of identified enhancers (union).
An enhancer is counted as active in a sample if it has a non-zero TSS signal on at least one strand in that sample.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
enh_count_plot <- readRDS("enhancer_count_per_sample_plot.rds")
enh_count_plot
```

### Annotation of enhancers
ChIPseeker annotation of genomic regions where enhancers reside, relative to the transcripts annotated in the user-provided GTF file.
Two parameters should be defined for this step: `tssregion_up` and `tssregion_down`.
They correspond to the upstream and downstream distance from the TSS of *an annotated* transcript to include into the TSS region for ChIPseeker annotation.
`tssregion_up` should be negative, `tssregion_down` should be positive.
These parameters are shared with the tag cluster annotation.
While enhancers called within consensus tag clusters are excluded, some of the remaining enhancers may still fall into the promoter region defined by the `tssregion_up` and `tssregion_down` parameters. Therefore, the annotation below may show "promoter" categories for enhancers.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
print(paste0("The current tssregion_up value is: ", tssregion_up))
print(paste0("The current tssregion_down value is: ", tssregion_down))

enh_annot_plot <- readRDS("chipseeker_enhancer_annotation_plot.rds")
enh_annot_plot
```

### PCA plot of samples, based on enhancer expression
PCA of samples, calculated on the TPM values of the top 500 most variable enhancers across samples. 
If fewer than 500 enahncers are available, all enhancers are used.
The variance explained by each principal component is shown in parentheses.

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
enh_p_plot <- readRDS("enhancer_expression_pca_plot.rds")
enh_p_plot
```
